Hot Air Balloon Patterns Worksheet for Age 4

Age 4 YearsClass 25 · ShapesType Printable PDFPlays with <a href="/preschool/shapes/adventures/hot-air-balloon-patterns/">the online game</a>

AB and AAB patterns to finish with a pencil: say the pattern out loud, then draw what lands next.

On the sheet: Finish each pattern row: draw or color the shape that comes next.

THE ACTUAL WORKSHEET

Exactly what you’ll print.

This is the real sheet — the same file the buttons above hand you. Title, instructions, the activity itself, and a grown-up answer line where it helps.

Download Free Worksheet ↓ Play This Activity Online ↗

The PDF is a real printable file (A4, prints fine on US Letter). The print button prints only the worksheet — never the website around it. No sign-up, nothing stored.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Patterns are the first real maths rhythm. On paper your child reads the row left to right, says the pattern like a little song, and draws or colors the missing shape. The game plays the same way on screen — the sheet just slows it down and adds pencil control.

  • Reading a row left to right
  • Hearing and continuing AB and AAB patterns
  • Predicting what comes next and committing to it
  • Drawing small shapes with growing control
HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Read the sheet together

    Read the title and instructions aloud, then let your child explain back what the sheet asks for. Four-year-olds understand far more than they can read.

  2. Do the first one together

    Help with row one so the task is clear, then step back. A wrong line is information, not a mistake — talk about it and try again.

  3. Stop while it is fun

    One finished sheet is a full session. Hang it up, date the corner, and come back to a fresh copy of the same worksheet another day.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Chunky tools win

Thick crayons and stubby pencils fit four-year-old hands. Skinny pencils make small hands grip too hard.

Say the shape names out loud

Naming while doing — “a circle for the porthole!” — is what makes the learning stick.

Cutting counts as learning

The cut-and-sort sheets practice scissor control too. Snip along the dotted line together if scissors are new.

Answer guide

Row 1 continues circle, square, circle, square — the missing cell is a circle. Row 2 continues star, star, heart — the missing cell is a heart. (The game’s balloon rows follow the same AB and AAB rules.)

WHERE THIS FITS

The class and the game behind it.

This worksheet is the paper twin of Hot Air Balloon Patterns, a real game in the Shape Adventures library. It belongs to Shapes, Patterns & Sorting (Class 25) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole shapes collection lives at /worksheets/shapes/. Play the game on screen first, print the worksheet second — or the other way round; they practice the same skill in two languages.
